4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle) said Friday that his availability for Sunday's game against the Broncos remains up in the air, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4432665.story: "We still have some conversations to have, so we'll see," Bowers said. With the tight end already slated to carry a questionable tag into the weekend, his own comments don't provide added clarity about whether he'll suit up Sunday. The Raiders may wait until closer to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff before making a final call on Bowers' status. Jack Bech was the big winner in terms of playing time and targets after Bowers left last Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

4432665.headline: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4432665.story: Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4432665.story: After not practicing Wednesday, Bowers logged a limited session Thursday, and the tight end's presence on the field again Friday offers hope that he'll be able to give it a go Sunday against the Broncos. Per Warren, Bowers sported a wrap on his injured right ankle Friday, with his official participation level and game status set to arrive once the Raiders' Week 11 injury report comes out later in the day.

4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
4432665.story: Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end doesn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers already has cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

4689936.story: Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.

4689936.headline: Bates made two of his three field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Lions' 19-15 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
4689936.story: Bates converted field goals from 25 yards and 37 yards while missing a 46-yarder in the third quarter off the left upright. The kicker now is 12-for-13 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 23-for-23 on PATs through seven regular-season games in 2026.

4689936.headline: Bates went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
4689936.story: Bates was able to convert multiple field-goal attempts for just the second time this season. The kicker split the uprights on a 40-yard try in the second quarter before he sent Green Bay packing with a game-winning 22-yard chip shot as time expired in regulation. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, going 10-for-10 on field-goal tries, including a 54-yard make in Week 4 against the Panthers, while nailing all 22 of his extra-point attempts over six contests.

Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

How he fares in drills Thursday and Friday likely will determine if he's cleared to return to action Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

16737.headline: San Francisco general manager John Lynch said that "there's a chance" Evans (Achilles) will take part in a padded practice Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
16737.story: Evans joined up with the 49ers in Colorado Springs on Wednesday as the team began prepping for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City, but the wideout was merely a spectator for the first Week 11 practice. The veteran wideout looks as though he could see some involvement in drills Thursday, which would mark his first on-field activity since Week 6. Evans has been sidelined for the 49ers' past three games after aggravating a right Achilles injury in an Oct. 19 win over the Commanders.

4241985.story: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

4241985.headline: Why Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is primed to be Denver's primary running back
4241985.story:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- In the weeks before the 2026 NFL draft, there was a scout or two who classified Jonah Coleman as a "than" player.

They thought that Coleman, then a running back from the University of Washington, was faster than, more elusive than and a better receiver than many thought.

The early returns say the fourth-round rookie, whose current résumé consists of 39 touches through eight g

4241985.headline: Dobbins carried the ball seven times for 13 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
4241985.story: While the veteran RB got the start, by the end of the game Dobbins had fully given way to rookie Jonah Coleman, who wound up delivering 104 scrimmage yards on 15 touches and scored the game-winning touchdown. With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, Dobbins will still have a role in the Denver backfield, but Coleman made a compelling case Sunday to become the team's new No. 1 back. Dobbins should at least be more productive in Week 9, even on limited volume, against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.

4241985.headline: Dobbins and Jonah Coleman will lead the Broncos' backfield against the Chiefs on Sunday due to the absence of RJ Harvey (knee), Eric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
4241985.story: Harvey popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a knee injury and was unable to practice Friday, which resulted in him being ruled out for Sunday's AFC West tilt. Dobbins found the end zone in Week 7 against the Cardinals but was less efficient with his carries than Coleman, although the duo could have a fairly even split in backfield duties in Harvey's absence. Through seven regular-season games. Dobbins has turned 87 carries into 293 yards (3.4 YPC) and three touchdowns while adding eight catches on nine targets for 27 yards.

12483.headline: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
12483.story: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 by

12483.headline: What to know to set your lineup: Cousins' Vikings return elevates Jefferson
12483.story: Have you ever been in a relationship that was so bad, you yearned for the one who got away? Because if you did, you might just be the Minnesota Vikings. And that bad relationship might be with Carson Wentz. Just kidding. It was with Wentz. And the rift was very public, too, happening on "Monday Night Football."

12483.headline: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry.
12483.story: The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

12483.headline: Bowen: Six players you can now trust in lineups, four that you cannot any longer
12483.story:
Everyone has some level of trust issues with their fantasy football roster.

Maybe it's that flex spot in your lineup, the one you flip on a weekly basis, rotating between a big play wide receiver or a running back who can give you some passing-game upside. The quarterbacks? I'm there right now in one of my leagues, arguing (with myself) on which fringe QB1 I'm going to start this week. Just give me the 16-18 points I need to win.

So, that got me thinking about the players we can trust, and th

4426385.story: With the Indianapolis Colts releasing Daniel Jones, the team will start Anthony Richardson Sr. for the Week 12 matchup versus the

4426385.headline: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
4426385.story: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

4426385.headline: Fantasy football: Which players can you trust from these backfields-by-committee?
4426385.story:
The lack of quality running back depth has been an issue for fantasy football managers this year, and it's even tougher to find consistent production in the lineup with so many shared backfields across the league.

That got us thinking about how managers can approach teams that are using two backs, as it pertains to setting a weekly lineup (across multiple formats).

4426385.headline: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
4426385.story: The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

4428718.headline: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
4428718.story: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

4428718.headline: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
4428718.story: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

4428718.headline: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
4428718.story: Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Fran

4428718.headline: Tucker secured five of 12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
4428718.story: Tucker led the Raiders in receiving yards and targets on the afternoon with a big lift from a game-long 41-yard catch and a 37-yard fourth-quarter touchdown reception. The speedy wideout has a combined 10-200-3 line over his last two games alone as he continues to take his chemistry with Kirk Cousins to new levels, and Tucker is averaging a stellar 16.3 yards per reception heading into a favorable Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

4686361.headline: Little went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs during Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
4686361.story: Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.

4686361.headline: Little made all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries in a 33-10 win over Baltimore on Thursday.
4686361.story: The Jaguars dominated in the victory, but they fell short of the end zone enough times to keep Little busy. He didn't need to fully flex the strength of his leg, as his longest kick was from a modest 47 yards out, but Little extended his run of consecutive successful FG attempts to 10. He's now gone 14-of-16 on field-goal tries this season while converting 25 of 26 point-after attempts.

4686361.headline: Little nailed all six extra-point attempts in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
4686361.story: The kicker did not get a field-goal attempt, but he was the beneficiary of an offense that scored six touchdowns. Little has connected on 22 of 23 extra-point tries in 2026, though he has only 12 total field-goal attempts, 10 of which he's made.

4686361.headline: Little made his sole field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans on Sunday in London.
4686361.story: Little made a 60-yard field goal with 1:55 left in the fourth quarter to tie the game, 31-31. The Jaguars' kicker continues to deliver in big moments for the team whenever called upon. Little moves to 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-17 on PATs through six games in 2026.

15818.headline: Allen brought in five of seven targets for 61 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
15818.story: Allen looked rejuvenated in his 49ers debut after coming over from the Colts at the deadline, finishing third in receptions and receiving yards and second in targets for his new squad in the wild win. Allen and Brock Purdy seemed to have instant chemistry despite having practiced on only three occasions coming into the contest, and the veteran receiver's production should have a good chance of spiking further down the stretch of the regular season.

15818.headline: Allen will play for the 49ers in Sunday's game at Dallas after being acquired in a trade earlier this week, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
15818.story: Allen could have a significant role immediately, joining an injury-riddled WR room, though Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been cleared to play this Sunday. Mike Evans (Achilles) is out again, leaving Samuel, Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins as the top healthy options at wide receiver. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned Wednesday that Allen still has some risk of being suspended at some point this season due to an August arrest for DUI while he was with the Colts, per 95.7 The Game.

15818.headline: Fantasy impacts of the NFL trade deadline: Breaking down fantasy-relevant moves
15818.story:
Fantasy managers have their eyes on the prize as they hoped for new destinations for their beloved stars at the NFL trade deadline. Some players stayed put, some ended up in new cities and one ended the day back with familiar faces. What does it all mean going forward for managers and their rosters?

The ESPN fantasy football crew has you covered, breaking down what's in store for the new additions, as well as other players who are either stepping up or sharing the limelight. We tracked the latest news through the 4

15818.headline: The 49ers acquired Allen from the Colts on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
15818.story: A beat-up 49ers receiving corps will get some much-needed reinforcement in the form of Allen, who has still displayed the ability to move the chains during his age-34 season. Through eight games with the Colts, Allen produced a 40-351-1 receiving line on 58 targets. While Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) may be prioritized ahead of him in the passing game once fully healthy, Allen could have the opportunity to see steady target volume right out of the gate Sunday in Dallas.

3046779.headline: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
3046779.story: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

3046779.headline: Goff (chest) practiced fully Thursday.
3046779.story: Goff kicked off Week 10 prep as limited Wednesday due to a chest injury, but his return to all activity one day later puts him in the clear for Sunday's contest against the Patriots in Munich. He'll be taking on a New England defense that was just torched by Packers QB Jordan Love for 372 yards and three touchdowns in Week 9.

3046779.headline: Goff was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury.
3046779.story: Goff is making his first appearance on the injury report this season, but he at least logged some reps Wednesday as he tends to a health concern. A return to full participation Thursday and/or Friday should put him in the clear for Sunday's game versus the Patriots.

4371733.headline: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
4371733.story: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

4431452.headline: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
4431452.story: Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

4431452.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.
4431452.story: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to s

3916387.headline: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
3916387.story: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

3916387.headline: Jackson (thumb) is "doing well" and is expected to be out for "6-to-10 weeks," per head coach Jesse Minter.
3916387.story: Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was rece

3916387.headline: Jackson, who is scheduled to undergo surgery on his injured right thumb, has told teammates he plans to return later this season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
3916387.story: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a tu

3916387.headline: Jackson's odds to play again this season depend on his recovery from a right thumb injury, and also whether or not new QB Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens in the playoff picture long enough to make a return late in the season possible for Jackson, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
3916387.story: The Ravens already have cycled through three starting QBs this season, and with Tyler Huntley sidelined for the rest of the campaign due to a turf-toe injury and Jackson out indefinitely, the team agreed to a trade with the Cardinals for Brissett, which became official Friday. Brissett was serviceable until he wasn't in Arizona, finishing his 2026 season there with 1,719 yards on 63 percent passing, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight appearances, and he'll have top talents in RB Derrick Henry and WR Zay Flowers to work with in his new locale. It remains to be seen if Baltimore, whi

4832800.headline: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
4832800.story: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

4832800.headline: Boston (toe) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of The Athletic reports.
4832800.story: Boston missed practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but was able to log a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken being quoted as saying that the 2026 second-rounder was "trending in the right way" heading into the weekend. With his active status confirmed, in absence of any in-game limitations or setbacks, Boston is positioned to maintain his key role in a Cleveland WR corps that also features KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy. Through his first nine regular-season games as a pro, Boston leads him team with 507 receiving yards, while having hauled in 32 of his 60 targets in that span along

4832800.headline: Boston (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, is expected to play barring a surprise, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
4832800.story: After missing practice Wednesday and Thursday, Boston returned to a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken noting that the WR was "trending in the right way." Now, assuming no setbacks in warmups, it appears as though Boston will be available versus Houston, with his official game status set to be confirmed once Cleveland's inactives are posted about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1 pm ET kickoff.

4832800.headline: Boston (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN,  is trending in the right direction ahead of the contest.
4832800.story: With that in mind, coach Todd Monken noted Friday that Boston "moved around pretty good...it's trending in the right way." It's worth noting, however, that Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer relays that Boston left the team's locker room in a walking boot, but it's possible that's simply a precautionary measure. Either way, the wideout's Week 10 status will be known prior to the first batch of games Sunday, with the Browns kicking off at 1:00 pm ET. 3128429.story: The conundrum picking Broncos' wide receivers in fantasy

3128429.headline: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
3128429.story: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
3128429.story: For the fourth straight game, Sutton failed to see more than five targets, but his four grabs and 53 yards were both season highs. It's been a rough campaign so far for the 31-year-old receiver in an inconsistent Broncos aerial attack, and Sutton will take a 20-221-1 line on 37 targets through eight games intro a Week 9 clash with the Panthers.

4373678.headline: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
4373678.story: With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

4373678.headline: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
4373678.story: Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

4373678.headline: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
4373678.story: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.

4373678.headline: Shakir brought in four of six targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
4373678.story: Shakir posted his second-lowest yardage figure of the season, but the talented veteran recorded his first touchdown of the campaign on a nine-yard grab just past the midway point of the second quarter. His target total also tied for his second highest of the campaign, a figure he'd reached on two other occasions. The fifth-year pro should continue to garner his fair share of Josh Allen's attention moving forward, although Shakir's targets could take a slight hit if DJ Moore (shoulder) returns for a Week 8 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

2473037.headline: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
2473037.story: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

2473037.headline: Myers made his only field-goal attempt and converted both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
2473037.story: The Seahawks' offense put forth a relatively modest showing in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock (oblique) at the helm, but Myers made good on the few opportunities that he did have, rebounding somewhat from a rough game in Week 8 where he missed two kicks. Starting quarterback Sam Darnold (quadriceps) will again be out in Week 10 at Las Vegas, but Myers will at least have the benefit of kicking indoors come Sunday.

2473037.headline: Myers missed his lone field-goal attempt and made one of two PATs in Monday night's 34-17 loss to the Bears.
2473037.story: Myers converted a chip-shot 27-yard field goal in the second quarter but later missed an extra point wide to the left before halftime. He then had a 33-yard field-goal try blocked in the fourth quarter. On the season, the veteran kicker is 14-for-16 on FGAs and 17-for-19 on PATs. He'll be a kicker to stream next Sunday at home against the Cardinals.

2473037.headline: Myers went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday night's 20-3 win over the Chiefs.
2473037.story: Myers was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game, converting a 25-yarder in the second quarter before later adding a 35-yard make in the second half. The kicker has now gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 campaign.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
4362081.story: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

4362081.headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
4362081.story: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
4362081.story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

4362081.headline: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
4362081.story: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

3055899.headline: Butker made all five PATs in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
3055899.story: Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

3055899.headline: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
3055899.story: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.

3055899.headline: Butker missed his only field-goal attempt and made all five of his PATs during Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
3055899.story: Butker pushed his only field-goal try wide right from 51 yards out in the final moments of the first half. The kicker has now gone 12-for-19 on field-goal attempts this season, and head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker's future following the game, stating that he'll "address that" as the team prepares for Week 10, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. The team signed veteran Justin Tucker to the practice squad in late October, and Tucker could get a shot with the active roster in Butker's place.

3055899.headline: Head coach Andy Reid said that Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker for Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
3055899.story: Butker -- who has made 12 of his 18 field-goal attempts in seven games this season -- converted one of his two tries along with with all three point-after attempts in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. Despite his recent accuracy issues, Butker will retain his kicking role this weekend, even though the Chiefs recently signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Colts.
4432708.story: Harrison was also inactive for this past Sunday's game against the Browns, and he will now target a potential return to action Nov. 29 versus the Ravens following Houston's Week 11 bye. In his continued absence, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell will handle the Texans' WR duties Thursday. Collins (16 targets, nine catches) and Hutchinson (nine targets, four catches) combined for 152 receiving yards on the 25 targets the duo saw against Cleveland in Week 10.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.
4432708.story: While the Texans haven't provided a definitive word on Harrison's status for Thursday's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston relays that the 24-year-old wideout is trending toward missing a second straight contest now that he's yet to practice in any fashion this week. Since being acquired from the Cardinals in October, Harrison has suited up in three games for Houston and has recorded six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant on Monday's practice report.
4432708.story: After missing Sunday's loss to the Browns, Harrison opened the new week with another missed practice due to his hamstring issue. If he's unable to return in time for Thursday night's game against the Colts on a short week, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell likely will soak up the vast majority of the snaps at wideout.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
4432708.story: Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
4432710.story: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

4432710.headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Henderson (illness) is working hard to get back, while acknowledging that he doesn't have a timetable for when that may occur, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
4432710.story: On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings r

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) didn't practice Wednesday and is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
4432710.story: Henderson was one of three players listed as out for this weekend's contest, signaling that they are not in line to make the trip to Germany. With Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) not practicing Wednesday and reportedly on track to miss some time, it looks like Corey Kiner is trending toward leading New England's Week 10 backfield, with Lan Larison also in the mix and Terrell Jennings a potential practice-squad elevation. New England has a bye in Week 11, so Nov. 29 against the Chargers is Henderson's soonest possible return date.

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) was absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
4432710.story: With Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) both absent, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are left as New England's top running backs ahead of a Week 10 matchup in Munich against the Lions on Sunday. After that, the Patriots have a Week 11 bye, and it's still unclear when Henderson might be available again.

4685261.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
4685261.story: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

4685261.headline: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
4685261.story: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

4685261.headline: Bernard caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
4685261.story: It was a big step back in production for the rookie wideout compared to Week 6 against the Bucs, but Bernard still ran a team-high 33 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 34 dropbacks against New Orleans. Bernard's role is secure while Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) remain sidelined for at least two more games each. Bernard will be a fantasy WR3 for next Sunday's game against the Browns.

4685261.headline: Fantasy football: Six surging players to believe in
4685261.story:
With a third of the NFL season in the books, now is a good time to examine players who are surging in usage and production. You can see it on the tape and in the elevated numbers. There are signs of really good football here, and we need to discuss why it will continue.

Today, let's look at six players climbing my rankings heading into Week 7. I have a quarterback on a three-game heater, a tight end who could finally be emerging after a disappointing start, and multiple wide receivers with defined roles in their respective offenses. These players need to be in lineups

4360078.headline: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
4360078.story: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

4360078.headline: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
4360078.story: Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

4360078.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
4360078.story: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

4360078.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) won't have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 7, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
4360078.story: Pierce now has spent the requisite four games on injured reserve after re-injuring his surgically repaired left heel in the Colts' Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, but he'll need some more time to complete a rehab program before getting back on the practice field. Given the recurring nature of Pierce's injury in addition to the significant financial investment in him, the Colts are likely to take a deliberate approach in bringing the wideout back from IR.

4249087.headline: Gay (hip) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4249087.story: The veteran kicker was able to practice Friday, which should make him better than 50/50 to kick against Denver. If he's unable to, Gay would likely be replaced by Kansei Matsuzawa.

4249087.headline: Gay (hip) was spotted at practice Friday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4249087.story: Gay, who was limited Wednesday, logged a DNP on Thursday, but it looks like he'll work in some capacity to close out the week. Per Warren, the Raiders worked out three kickers with Gay injured, but it appears as though it's only Gay and practice-squad member Kansei Matsuzawa available to handle kicks at Friday's practice.

4249087.headline: Gay (hip) didn't practice Thursday.
4249087.story: Gay was limited Wednesday, so the kicker's downgrade in participation a day later clouds his status for Sunday's game against the Broncos. With that in mind, the Raiders had Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo in for tryouts Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

4249087.headline: Gay (hip) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4249087.story: Gay made both of his two field-goal tries and his only extra-point attempt during Sunday's 21-13 loss versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have picked up a hip injury at some point along the way. As long as he can manage a full practice Thursday or Friday, he should still be in a good position to suit up in Week 11 against the Broncos.

4360761.headline: The Cardinals placed Wilson (neck) on injured reserve Tuesday.
4360761.story: Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three

4360761.headline: Coach Mike LaFleur revealed Monday that Wilson is out for the season due to a fracture in his neck, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
4360761.story: With the Cardinals' top WR now sidelined and presumably headed to season-ending IR, Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace and Devin Duvernay currently are the wide receivers on the team's active roster. Additionally, Shedrick Jackson, Zay Jones and James Proche are on Arizona's practice squad, but look for further reinforcements to be considered by the Cardinals in the coming days.

4360761.headline: Wilson notched six catches (on seven targets) for 60 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss in Seattle.
4360761.story: Wilson has been tending to two broken ribs the last two games, and he also was working with new starting QB Gardner Minshew after the Cardinals dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens this past week. Nonetheless, Wilson led Arizona in receiving yards, marking the fourth time he's reached 60 such yards in the last seven contests en route to a 38-412-2 line on 67 targets during that stretch. Wilson will look to improve his rapport with Minshew -- and also get healthier -- next Sunday versus the Rams.

4360761.headline: Wilson (rest/ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in Seattle, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
4360761.story: Wilson has worn a yellow non-contact jersey in practice the last two weeks due to two broken ribs -- a situation that contained him to limited sessions. Having said that, he'll continue to play through the concern as he did this past Sunday in Dallas, when he hauled in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown while adding one carry for 17 yards on a 79 percent snap share.

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
4361432.story: With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

4361432.headline: The Patriots placed Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve Monday.
4361432.story: Just after welcoming A.J. Brown back from IR in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, the Patriots will have another starting wideout in Doubs land on the shelf for at least the next four games. Doubs sustained the shoulder injury while making a diving 42-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter, with the Patriots ruling him out for the rest of the game shortly thereafter. Though the extent of his shoulder injury isn't fully known, Doubs won't be eligible for activation until after the team's Week 11 bye as a result of the transaction. Doubs' upcoming absence should open up more playing time for D

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
4361432.story: Doubs was injured on his 42-yard TD catch in the first quarter, after which he went to the sideline tent, and eventually, the locker room. A shoulder issue was the cause for his exit and will keep him out for the rest of Week 6. A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are the Patriots' remaining healthy and available wide receivers.

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
4361432.story: Doubs recorded a 42-yard touchdown connection with QB Drake Maye in the first quarter of Week 6 action, but he was shaken up afterward, visited the sideline tent and then went to the locker room before the Patriots deemed the wide receiver questionable to return. For as long as Doubs is off the field, A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will handle WR reps for New England.

3116165.headline: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
3116165.story: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

3116165.headline: NFL trade deadline: A Colts duo and others to keep tabs on for fantasy football
3116165.story:
The NFL trade deadline is around the corner, and it's when we start to separate the pretenders from the contenders. I have one question: Are we convinced that the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings are contenders?

Let's get into it, especially because the NFL's other unbeaten teams lost last week. The San Francisco 49ers b

3116165.headline: Godwin failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
3116165.story: The Bucs attempted three total passes in Sunday's rain-soaked conditions, and Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of the three. Instead, Tampa Bay ran the ball 56 times and coasted to an easy win on the backs of Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and the defense. Godwin will do battle with the Chicago secondary next Sunday, positioning the veteran wideout as a WR4 in fantasy. Emeka Egbuka (foot) could be back for that game after missing the past two contests.

3116165.headline: Godwin is in line to operate as the Buccaneers de facto No. 1 receiver again in Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Falcons, as Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is inactive for the contest per Scott Smith of the team's official site.
3116165.story: Godwin filled Egbuka's No. 1 role in a Week 7 rout of the Panthers, one where Baker Mayfield returned from a thumb injury but put the ball up only 11 times in a 43-13 win for Tampa Bay. As a result, Godwin ran just 12 routes, although he was targeted on 41.7 percent of them on his way to five targets and a 4-27-0 line. Considering Mayfield had just seven completions and 64 passing yards, Godwin's role was indeed that of the top option in the air attack, and Sunday's game against the Falcons is almost certain to involve appreciably higher passing volume for Tampa Bay.

4035687.headline: Pittman (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Mark Kaboly reports.
4035687.story: Pittman was designated for return from injured reserve earlier this week and had progressed to full participation Thursday, so his questionable tag keeps him in the mix for a potential activation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Eagles. With both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger) nearing a return, it's unclear what that will mean for rookie Germie Bernard's role going forward, as the rookie has hit a slow spot in the box score the last couple weeks.

4035687.headline: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
4035687.story: After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

4035687.headline: Pittman (foot) participated in practice Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
4035687.story: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman was able to return to a limited practice. The WR's presence at Thursday's session implies that there were no setbacks, with the Steelers' upcoming injury report set to reveal his official participation level. In any case, Pittman will need to be activated off IR no later than Saturday afternoon in order to have a chance to play Sunday against the Eagles.

4035687.headline: Pittman (foot) was limited in his return to practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
4035687.story: The Steelers could be poised to welcome back a pair of their key WRs to the lineup this week, with both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger, full practice) having been designated to return from IR on  Wednesday. Pittman who was placed on IR on Oct. 10, has played in three games so far in his first season with Pittsburgh and has recorded seven receptions for 89 yards on 12 targets in that span.

3929645.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
3929645.story: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

3929645.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Mendoza, Douglas, Estime among top options
3929645.story:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention who are available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

3929645.headline: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
3929645.story: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johns

3929645.headline: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
3929645.story: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

4038941.headline: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
4038941.story: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its c

4038941.headline: Five reasons why Chargers' offense, Justin Herbert have struggled in 2026 season
4038941.story:
Could it get any worse than this for the Chargers? After nine weeks, they are the only winless team in the NFL. They're the first team in NFL history to start 0-8 after winning 11-plus games in the previous season, per ESPN Research. And they haven't won a game since Week 16 of last season -- 331 days ago.

While last week's 44-22 loss to Houston featured plenty of poor defensive play,

4038941.headline: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
4038941.story: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

4038941.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports.
4038941.story: Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in inter

4837248.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Replacing Drake Maye? Trust in Tyson?
4837248.story: The New England Patriots are one of six teams that will not be playing in Week 11, as bye weeks continue. However, even when the defending AFC champions resume playing in Week 12 versus the Los Angeles Chargers, QB

4837248.headline: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
4837248.story: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

4837248.headline: Why the Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter
4837248.story:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- There isn't a particular moment that convinced the Las Vegas Raiders players and coaches that No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was ready to be the team's starting quarterback. It's a collection of things the rookie has done since he arrived at the facility in April.

For coach Klint Kubiak, it's M

4837248.headline: Don't be surprised if Jordan Love makes history and Mendoza performs like a QB1
4837248.story:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

15864.headline: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
15864.story: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

15864.headline: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
15864.story: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

15864.headline: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
15864.story: Smith also was deemed limited on Wednesday's practice estimate, so he may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Chargers without an injury designation. For his part, the Jets' QB1 isn't worried about his Week 11 availability, with Rich Cimini of ESPN.com noting Wednesday that while Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp at that point, the signal-caller stated that he intends to play this weekend. "That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

15864.headline: Smith (ankle), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, said afterward that he intends to play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
15864.story: Beyond noting that Smith will start if healthy, head coach Aaron Glenn hasn't confirmed that Smith will be available this weekend, but the quarterback's ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday is at least an encouraging sign for his status. Cimini notes that Smith was walking with a noticeable limp three days after injuring his left ankle in a Week 10 loss to the Bills, so the veteran signal-caller's mobility could be compromised to some degree if he gets the green light to play against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line for his first NFL start in the event Smith isn't d

4433970.story: The New England Patriots are one of six teams that will not be playing in Week 11, as bye weeks continue. However, even when the defending AFC champions resume playing in Week 12 versus the Los Angeles Chargers, QB

4433970.headline: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
4433970.story: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

4433970.headline: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports.
4433970.story: McCarthy missed much of the third quarter of this past Sunday's win at Philadelphia due to a hip pointer but was able to return to action, completing 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing four times for 22 yards. Considering he ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, he seemingly was in the clear for Thursday's matchup, and Palmer's report indicates McCarthy will take on every rep, leaving Jameis Winston as the No. 2 QB, and on the sidelines Thursday.

4433970.headline: McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
4433970.story: McCarthy was sidelined for most of the third quarter of this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles after sustaining a painful hip pointer, but he was able to finish out the game. Head coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence afterward that the injury wouldn't be anything that jeopardized McCarthy's status for Thursday's game against the Commanders, and the quarterback's ability to take every rep Tuesday clears the way for him to start on a short week. Through two starts and two appearances off the bench with the Giants, McCarthy has completed 43 of 68 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 622 yar

3052587.headline: Mayfield (foot/thumb) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Detroit.
3052587.story: Mayfield came out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye with a foot injury that sidelined him at Wednesday's practice. He proceeded to be a limited participant Thursday and Friday, and after the latter session, head coach Todd Bowles told Scott Smith of the team's official site that Mayfield "looked good" and is trending toward starting Sunday. Ultimately, Mayfield's status for Week 11 will be confirmed about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

3052587.headline: Mayfield (foot) is trending in the right direction to start Sunday's game against the Lions after looking good in Friday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
3052587.story: With Mayfield back on the field again Friday after managing the foot issue earlier this week, Tampa Bay appears to be gaining optimism about its starting quarterback's availability for Sunday's matchup. His official game designation for Sunday still will be key, but coach Todd Bowles' comments point toward Mayfield having a chance to avoid another absence.

3052587.headline: Mayfield (foot) is practicing again Friday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
3052587.story: With Mayfield having progressed from sitting out Wednesday to being limited Thursday, Friday's participation is another positive sign for his availability Sunday against Detroit. The Buccaneers' upcoming injury report is destined to reveal both Mayfield's participation level Friday, as well as his Week 11 game status.

3052587.headline: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) officially was limited at Thursday's practice.
3052587.story: Mayfield came out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye with a foot injury, which kept him out of drills Wednesday. After resuming on-field work Thursday, he relayed to Scott Smith of the team's official site that he felt good and was "limited," the latter of which has been confirmed. Per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano, Mayfield also said, "If I feel like [Jalon Daniels] gives us a better chance to win, I have no shame in admitting that." As a result, it appears as if both Mayfield and Daniels have a chance to be under center for Tampa Bay on Sunday at Detroit.

4360698.headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
4360698.story: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants

4360698.headline: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
4360698.story: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 by

4360698.headline: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
4360698.story: Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

4360698.headline: Milton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
4360698.story: The Eagles signed Milton off the practice squad to the active roster Friday following the news that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, with the latter being placed on injured reserve Saturday. The Eagles will start Tanner McKee on Sunday while rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton serves as the backup. As the emergency QB3, Milton is prohibited from playing against Carolina unless both McKee and Payton leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

2578570.headline: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
2578570.story: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects

2578570.headline: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
2578570.story: Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.

3917792.headline: Jones will be waived by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
3917792.story: Following Thursday's loss to Houston, James Boyd of The Athletic relayed that Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that he planned to "evaluate everything" in terms of the team's QB situation going forward. Now, as a result of Friday's decision, the team's new starter ahead of Week 12 action is Anthony Richardson, per Schefter.
